topic: How does the transceiver's variable gain distribution between RF and baseband impact dynamic range and noise performance trade-offs in different satellite orbital configurations?
consensus_response: The transceiver's variable gain distribution between RF and baseband significantly impacts dynamic range and noise performance trade-offs in different satellite orbital configurations. In Low Earth Orbit (LEO), a higher pre-amplifier gain reduces the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), increasing susceptibility to interference, while in Geostationary (GEO) and Medium Earth Orbit (MEO), non-linearities introduce additional noise and interference patterns, reducing capacity budget. Digital Pre-Distortion (DPD) can mitigate these effects by compensating for array factor effects, increasing capacity budget by up to 15% in LEO.
